methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free AI workshops led by a local native directly target capability distribution outside traditional tech hubs, signaling grassroots peer-to-peer knowledge transfer that could build deep fluency in underserved communities if sustained.

signals.title: New partnership between VCU and AI Ready RVA aims to boost AI education, innovation and community impact - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: The VCU-AI Ready RVA partnership creates institutional infrastructure for community-wide AI education beyond elite universities, attempting to distribute deep capability through deliberate partnership rather than market concentration.

signals.title: Roanoke College launches WorkAI Lab to prepare leaders for new era of technology - Roanoke College
signals.signal_reading: Roanoke College's WorkAI Lab signals emerging capability pockets in smaller metros, but its institutional focus on 'preparing leaders' suggests concentration within educated professional classes rather than broad community distribution.

signals.title: New Jersey, Virginia Can Lead the Nation By Building ‘AI Resilience Cohorts’ to Develop Early-Career, State Talent Pipelines - Federation of American Scientists
signals.signal_reading: The proposed AI Resilience Cohorts represent intentional policy design to distribute deep capability through early-career talent pipelines, directly counteracting the natural gravity of NoVA concentration if implemented across regions.

signals.title: In the data center capital of the world, residents ask who the AI boom is helping - NBC News
signals.signal_reading: Residents questioning who benefits from the AI boom in the data center capital reveals concentrated infrastructure producing neither local capability nor shared prosperity—physical presence without knowledge distribution or economic access.
